transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
President Trump is lashing out at Ukraine's President Zelensky,
blaming Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil infrastructure for high global diesel prices.
As NPR's Tamara Keith reports, this comes one day after the president had what he called
a highly successful discussion with Russia's President Putin.
After the call with Putin, Trump announced Russia would be sending diesel to the U.S. for purchase,
something the president said he hoped would bring down prices for farmers and truckers.
This is a reversal of U.S. policy meant to put pressure on Russia to end its war against Ukraine,
and required the U.S. Treasury to temporarily halt sanctions on Russian diesel.
Speaking to reporters outside the White House, Trump expressed anger with Ukraine's President Zelensky.
I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal, because he could have made many deals that for some reason he never does.
And to drive it home, Trump added, quote, "I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president."
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
A weakening Hurricane Isaiasus, now a post-tropical cyclone, is being blamed for at least four deaths.
The storm ran through Alabama after making landfall on the Florida coast last night.
NPR's Bill Chappelle has the latest.
One person died when a tree fell on a home in Escambia County, Florida.
That's just west of where Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 storm in the western Florida panhandle.
Another person died in Birmingham, Alabama.
Here's Jefferson County Emergency Management Agency Director Jim Coker.
We did have a storm-related fatality overnight.
A tree did fall on a house.
Isaias weakened into a post-tropical cyclone on Saturday, but its heavy rains could continue to cause flash flooding.
It's also bringing strong thunderstorms and potentially tornadoes to areas far from the Gulf Coast.
Bill Chappelle, NPR News.
Christa Pike, who survived a botched execution in Tennessee, has been discharged from the hospital and is back in prison.
NPR's Chantalice Duster has more.
Attorneys for death row inmate Christa Pike said Saturday that she has been discharged from a hospital
and returned to Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Tennessee.
Pike had been hospitalized after she received and survived two lethal doses of the sedative pentobarbital.
Her attorneys said in a statement that she is receiving medical care at the prison and that they are tracking her recovery.
The statement said Pike is "grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances."
Chantalice Duster, NPR News.
President Trump says he is evaluating whether the U.S. should join Saudi strikes against Iran-Bakuti rebels in Yemen.
The president commented after another attack on Saudi Arabia's airport in Riyadh.
You're listening to NPR.
Some Chesapeake Bay oyster farmers and harvesters are getting a boost from robots.
NPR's Ari Daniel introduces us to an engineer at the University of Maryland who's finding new uses for aquatic robots.
Oyster reefs used to abound in the Chesapeake, but over-harvesting decimated their ranks.
Watermen faced the daunting task of knowing when and where to harvest the adults.
Mechanical engineer Meow Yoo says the water is so murky that the effort tends to be a stab in the dark.
Our goal is to transform that guesswork into precision.
So she and her team scan the seabed using sonar and video footage from a raft-like surface robot and a smaller underwater robot.
They then use AI to stitch the visuals together and analyze them to determine if oysters are present and alive and how big they are.
They're still refining the algorithms, but use hoping the technology might one day be modified and scaled nationally.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
Venture capitalists and AI founders attending Tech Week in San Francisco have been praising the White House's hands-off approach to AI regulation.
President Trump recently hosted Tech Leaders in Washington, signing a voluntary safety pact for AI.
The pact encourages AI labs to self-monitor, but it lacks detailed safety measures.
These lack of safety requirements comes as some tech companies have revealed troubling hacking incidents involving their own AI models.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
